question.text: Wavelengths belonging to Balmer series lying in the range of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>450</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>750</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> were used to eject photoelectrons from a metal surface whose work function is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi></math>. Find (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>eV</mi></math>) the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons. (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>h</mi><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1242</mn><mo> </mo><mi>eV</mi><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math>.)

solution.text:
Wavelengths corresponding to minimum wavelength (λmin ) or maximum energy will emit photoeiectrons having kinetic energy which is maximum. (λmin ) belonging to Balmer series and Lying in the given range (450 nm to 750 nm) corresponds to transition from (n = 4 to n = 2). Here,

E⁡ 4 = - 1 3 · 6 4 2 = - 0 · 8 5  eV

and E⁡ 2 = - 1 3 · 6 2 2 = - 3 · 4  eV

∴ Δ E⁡ = E⁡ 4 - E⁡ 2 = 2 · 5 5  eV

K⁡ max = Energy of photon - work function = 2 · 5 5 - 2 · 0 = 0 · 5 5 eV
